Side A · Recipe 02

Frozen sky

Ambient pad you can play after it's frozen

A slow chord that rises into a shimmering cathedral, then freezes in place. You turn one knob and the frozen sky moves up or down in semitones, like playing a second instrument.

Level
Easy
Setup
10 min
Key
A minor, chords Am and F
  1. What you'll hear
  2. 1. PERfourMER: a three-voice pad
  3. 2. Grand Canyon: a slow wobble
  4. 3. NightSky: the cathedral

What you'll hear

A soft three-voice chord, slowly wobbling. The reverb climbs an octave on every pass, like a choir. Then you freeze it, and turn the frozen cloud up and down while the bass keeps going.

The trick: the NightSky's SIZE/PITCH knob also changes the pitch of audio it's holding. Freeze a chord, and that knob becomes a transpose control.

1. PERfourMER: a three-voice pad

Put synth channels 1, 3 and 4 on MIDI channel 1 (see the rig page), and set PLAYMODE to P1: those three channels now play chords. Set all three the same:

  • PLAYMODEM1M2P1P2D1D2Poly 1: each note of a chord gets its own channel, up to three here.
  • WAVEsinetrianglesquaresawnoiseEXTFull and warm once filtered.
  • OCTAVE8'Middle register.
  • CUTOFF10 o'clockFairly closed: soft.
  • RESONANCE9 o'clockBarely.
  • Filter LFO INT9 o'clockThe LFO moves the filter a little: the pad breathes.
  • LFO WAVES&Hsinesaw or squareA smooth sweep.
  • LFO SPEED/PHASE9 o'clockSlow.
  • VCA MODEEGGATEONThe envelope shapes the volume.
  • ATTACK1 o'clockSlow fade-in: no attack at all.
  • DECAYnoonGentle.
  • SUSTAIN2 o'clockThe chord holds while the note is held.
  • RELEASE2 o'clockA long fade when the chord ends.
  • PANnoonIn the main left output, which feeds the pedals.

2. Grand Canyon: a slow wobble

  • DELAY TYPEMODDigital delay with a moving delay time: chorus and vibrato.
  • DELAY7:30 o'clockNear the minimum: you hear thickness, not echoes. If you hear separate echoes, turn it further left.
  • FEEDBACK9 o'clockVery few repeats.
  • MOD RATE (left mini knob)9 o'clockSlow movement.
  • MOD DEPTH (right mini knob)11 o'clockA wobble you feel more than hear.
  • DELAY LVL11 o'clockUnder the dry signal: a thickener.
  • PING PONGoffonRepeats alternate left and right: wider.

3. NightSky: the cathedral

  • TEXTUREsparsedensediffusePlate-like and dense; at long decays it turns ambient.
  • LENGTH3 o'clockVery long tail.
  • SHIMMER (button)inputregenShimmer inside the core: each pass climbs again, ascending as it decays.
  • INTERVALmax+1 octave: the choir rises in octaves.
  • SHIMMER (knob)10 o'clockA little shimmer goes a long way.
  • GLIMMERhighlowoffA washy, dreamy top end.
  • QUANTIZEsmoothhalf stepscaleSIZE/PITCH moves in semitones: needed for the trick in step 5.
  • SIZE/PITCHnoonThe middle of the range: no pitch change yet.
  • FILTERregenlow passThe tail darkens as it fades, so the shimmer doesn't pile up.
  • HIGH CUT1 o'clockKeep some sparkle.
  • LOW CUT10 o'clockLeaves room for the bass.
  • TARGETverbpitchfilterModulation moves the reverb itself.
  • SHAPEtrianglesquarerampsawrandomenvEven.
  • SPEED9 o'clockSlow.
  • DEPTH9 o'clockSubtle.
  • DRYnoonUnity.
  • REVERB2 o'clockThe cloud is the main sound here.

4. The OXI One: play it

Sequencer 1 in Poly mode on Ch 1; sequencer 2 Mono on Ch 2 for the bass.

  1. Tempo around 70 BPM: hold Shift, turn knob 1.
  2. Sequencer 1: on step 1, tap three pads in the same column: a chord (for example A, C, E). Up to seven notes fit on one step.
  3. Make the chord last the whole bar: for each note of the chord, hold its pad on step 1 and tap the same row on the bar's last step. That ties that note across the bar.
  4. Make a second chord a bar later (F, A, C), tied the same way.
  5. Sequencer 2 (the bass patch from the rig page): the root of each chord, A then F, low, tied across the bar.

You got it right when

  • The chord rises an octave in the reverb as it fades.
  • After INFINITE, the cloud stays when the chord stops.
  • Turning SIZE/PITCH moves the frozen cloud in clean semitone steps.

5. The performance: freeze and transpose

  1. Let a chord ring, then press INFINITE. The cloud holds.
  2. Turn SIZE/PITCH. With QUANTIZE on half step it moves in semitones. Counter-clockwise goes up, clockwise goes down, up to an octave each way. (The manual: minimum is up, maximum is down.)
  3. Stop sequencer 1 first (the factory setting lets new chords pour into the frozen cloud). Then try +5 (a fourth) and +7 (a fifth) semitones over the bass: they usually fit.
  4. Bring it back to noon, then press INFINITE again to let the sky melt away.

If it sounds wrong

  • The frozen cloud doesn't move: QUANTIZE is on scale with a scale that skips that note, or SIZE/PITCH is back at noon.
  • Too bright, almost a whistle: SHIMMER knob down, or HIGH CUT left.
  • Chords cut off: with three voices, a fourth note steals the oldest. Keep chords to three notes.

Sources

  • NightSky manual: TEXTURE and SIZE/PITCH, including "adjusting SIZE/PITCH will change the pitch of the reverberated audio" (pp. 5–6), QUANTIZE ranges (p. 6), shimmer and INTERVAL (p. 8), GLIMMER (p. 9), INFINITE (p. 18).
  • Grand Canyon manual: MOD delay type (p. 17), PING PONG (p. 11).
  • PERfourMER MKII manual: combining channels and PLAYMODE P1 (pp. 25–27), LFO (p. 16).
  • OXI One MKII manual: Poly sequencer, chords and ties (p. 132).
